Topics · Death and what comes after

Does karma work like gravity, or like a judge?

Gravity ignores motive. What weighs intention? The Quran says that takes knowing, and this judge forgives.

Part 1 of 3

﴿فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُۥ٧ وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُۥ٨﴾

Translation of the meaning

So whoever does an atom's weight[1965] of good will see it, And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.

Translator's notes

[1965] Or "the weight of a small ant."

Quran · Az-Zalzalah 99:7-8

Translation

For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it is good, or whether it is evil.

Original · Hebrew

כִּ֤י אֶת־כָּל־מַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים יָבִ֥א בְמִשְׁפָּ֖ט עַ֣ל כָּל־נֶעְלָ֑ם אִם־ט֖וֹב וְאִם־רָֽע׃

Ecclesiastes · 12:14

World English Bible

The verse says of the smallest acts what kamma says: whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of harm will see that. That exactness you describe is common ground: nothing is lost. What remains is the question you asked: how does the exactness work? Gravity is exact too, but look at what it acts on. It acts on mass, not on intention. A stone dropped in anger and one dropped in play fall alike.

A question for you

Which is closer to what you picture of kamma: gravity, or a judge?

If you sayGravity: it works by itself
ThenGravity is exact, but it does not act on intention. Two stones fall alike in anger and in play. Kamma as taught tells them apart. The next verse asks what that telling-apart would require.
If you sayA judge: someone weighs
ThenAn ordinary judge errs, can be bribed, and tires. What you describe does none of these. So what kind of judge is this? The next verse speaks to that.
If you sayNeither, something else
ThenThen set your picture beside the verses ahead and see where they touch and where they part. That is more honest than a ready-made choice.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِۦ نَفْسُهُۥ ۖ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We have already created man and know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer[1528] to him than [his] jugular vein.

Translator's notes

[1528] In absolute knowledge of everything about him. "We" has also been interpreted to mean the angels who are mentioned in the following verse.

Quran · Qaf 50:16

Translation

You are near, Yahweh. All your commandments are truth.

Original · Hebrew

קָר֣וֹב אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה וְֽכָל־מִצְוֺתֶ֥יךָ אֱמֶֽת׃

the Psalms · 119:151

World English Bible

If kamma weighs intention, it must reach inside, where no one else can see. A Buddhist may reply that intention shapes the mind that holds it, as a seed grows by its nature, so nothing needs to read it. That is a careful teaching on how character grows. The verse adds its own word: the One knows what the soul whispers, and is nearer than the vein in the neck.

A question for you

Can a process be exact about intention without somehow registering it?

If you sayYes, the result just follows the intention
ThenThen the process responds to a mind as a mirror responds to a face. That is a fine picture of how a mind shapes itself. Hold it beside the verse, which speaks of One who knows.
If you sayNo, something must register it
ThenThat is what the verse says: something knows what is inside. After that the question remains: what is it, and what is its stance toward the one it weighs?
If you sayI do not know
ThenThe suttas report the Buddha counting the way kamma works among things not to be pursued by speculation. So you stand in an honest place, and the next verse offers what the Quran says on another side of the question.

Part 3 of 3

﴿قُلْ يَـٰعِبَادِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا۟ مِن رَّحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh forgives all sins.[1354] Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

Translator's notes

[1354] For those who repent and correct themselves.

Quran · Az-Zumar 39:53

Translation

Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts. Let him return to Yahweh, and he will have mercy on him, to our God, for he will freely pardon.

Original · Hebrew

יַעֲזֹ֤ב רָשָׁע֙ דַּרְכּ֔וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אָ֖וֶן מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֑יו וְיָשֹׁ֤ב אֶל־יְהוָה֙ וִֽירַחֲמֵ֔הוּ וְאֶל־אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ כִּֽי־יַרְבֶּ֥ה לִסְלֽוֹחַ׃

Isaiah · 55:7

World English Bible

A judge can pardon. The verse says those who have wronged themselves are not to despair of God's mercy, since He forgives sins altogether. So the verses describe One just and merciful: He knows the intention, weighs with exactness, and leaves the door open.

A question for you

Would you want the account to be kept by one who can forgive?

If you sayYes
ThenThat is what the verse says of this judge: no despair of His mercy, and He forgives sins altogether. It is an answer of hope, not of fear.
If you sayNo, a law is cleaner
ThenThat position has force: a law shows no favour. The Quran says elsewhere that no one is wronged in the weighing (21:47), and this verse adds mercy. The difference lies in what is added, not in the scale.
If you sayIt depends
ThenOn what? That is a question worth sitting with. The closing step asks you to say where you have come to.

The same in the other books

Translation

Also to you, Lord, belongs loving kindness, for you reward every man according to his work.

Original · Hebrew

וּלְךָֽ־אֲדֹנָ֥י חָ֑סֶד כִּֽי־אַתָּ֨ה תְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לְאִ֣ישׁ כְּֽמַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ׃

the Psalms · 62:12

World English Bible

Translation

If you say, “Behold, we didn’t know this,” doesn’t he who weighs the hearts consider it? He who keeps your soul, doesn’t he know it? Shall he not give to every man according to his work?

Original · Hebrew

כִּֽי־תֹאמַ֗ר הֵן֮ לֹא־יָדַ֪עְנ֫וּ זֶ֥ה הֲֽלֹא־תֹ֘כֵ֤ן לִבּ֨וֹת ׀ הֽוּא־יָבִ֗ין וְנֹצֵ֣ר נַ֭פְשְׁךָ ה֣וּא יֵדָ֑ע וְהֵשִׁ֖יב לְאָדָ֣ם כְּפָעֳלֽוֹ׃

Proverbs · 24:12

World English Bible

Let no man think lightly of evil, saying in his heart, It will not come nigh unto me. Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled; the fool becomes full of evil, even if he gather it little by little. Let no man think lightly of good, saying in his heart, It will not come nigh unto me. Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled; the wise man becomes full of good, even if he gather it little by little.

Buddhist texts · Dhp 121-122

Max Müller, 1881

Translation

Even so, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”

Original · Ancient Greek

οὕτως, λέγω ὑμῖν, γίνεται χαρὰ ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι.

the Gospel (Luke) · 15:10

World English Bible

If you knew your hidden intention was fully seen, would your actions change? How?
